Derek Williams, in only his third year of athletics, is not far away from International class. His best long jump of the year, 7.38 metres in the final Southern League match, missed our Club Record by just 3 centimetres.

The worst blow came when Derek Williams, down for five events and on whom we rely far too heavily, came out with a pulled hamstring. Nice to see Pat Halliday though, back from France for the weekend and turning up on the off-chance of a run.

Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton were 7th and 9th in the 3km and 10km walks, Derek Williams leaped a personal best of 7.21 and Ernest Obeng began his 1980 summer campaign by taking the 100 metre title in 10.53.
Derek Williams backed up well with a 1st and 2nd and also won a bet with Tom Carter when he comfortably took the long jump with well over 7 metres (the "stake" being a new measuring tape).
Olympic Trials on June 15th, Derek Williams hit 7.01 for a disappointing 10th in the long jump.
Outstanding was Derek Williams with 2nd in the 100, 200, triple jump, 1st in the long jump with a personal best and near league record, and the vital man in both relays (48.2 for the long one).

In the Sefton Brancker Trophy, competing for the Civil Service, on July 23rd, Derek Williams won the long jump in 7.14. He also won the Civil Service Championship at Cwmbran on August 13th, with 7.17 and placed 2nd over 400 metres in 50.0.
Impressive jumping by Club Champions Derek Williams and Dawn McNeil.

Derek Williams looked as though he was heading for a very good year after winning the Surrey Long Jump and coming second in the U.K. Championships, but injury struck yet again and he was sidelined for most of the season.
Derek Williams travelled to Antrim in N.Ireland on May 24th for the U.K.
Derek Williams competed in six events. Mark Shippen made a welcome return to finish 2nd in the pole-vault and Tom Dowdall ran himself into the ground to set a p.b. 3000 s.c.

Derek Williams competing in fewer events than usual (and due to the good support), took the opportunity to compete all jumps, ironically his 6th long jump, taken even though he was a clear winner, resulted in an injury which was to put him out for the rest of the season.

We expected to be out-classed by the 5 National League Clubs especially, as Derek Williams was injured, Ernest Obeng was on his overseas Tour and 2 of our Juniors were competing in a Home Counties International at Meadowbank while 3 other Juniors were running for Surrey in the Junior Inter-Counties at Brighton.

Derek Williams and John Aska were elected Track and Field Captains respectively and they fulfilled these roles admirably. Derek gave top class performances every time he competed and John played a vital role in our success all season and especially at Luton, even though he did not always compete himself.

Derek Williams was at his brilliant best as were Ken, Snowy, Vincent, Mark and sprinters Pat Lyttle and Mike Alleyne. Benny did his usual trick in the B 800 of being last with 200 to go.

We demolished the opposition with some out-standing performances from Ernest Obeng, Colin Gaynor and Derek Williams but the star of the meeting was Stu Paton with wins over International competition in the 800, 1500 and a superb run of 48.0 in the 400 Relay.

Derek Williams won the long jump with 7.31m.We were pleased to sign on Dr.Bob Hebble who ran the 3000 for London Univ. At the U.K.Chamionships held at Cwmbran on May 30/31st Derek Williams finished 5th in the long jump with 7.28.

Individual wins were also recorded by; Peter Gilbey- 3000 S/C- 9.29.3, Olly Foote- 10000m- 31.29, --- Derek Williams who won his first Decathlon with 5386 pts; and Paul Richley who won the Junior 3000m in 8.41.0

By the season's end 2 Vets records had been broken by Charlie Gillett and Bill Treharne; 7 Senior records had been either broken or equalled by John Gladwin, Mark L Bayley, Jim Gregg, Phil Lovell Derek Williams, Ken Onuagaluchi and the 4x400m squad of Guy Sagar, John Gladwin, Stuart Paton, and Dave Mote.

Other good performances came from Colin Gaynor, Derek Williams(5events), and Stuart Paton. The coach journey back to London was a happy affair with little regard for the terrible weather outside which had persisted all day.
Roy Vassall achieved 7.00 to beat Derek Williams in the long jump and Mark Shippen vaulted a pb 4.40. Many of the top GLC people attended and were appreciative of our efforts.
